overview: This Senate resolution mourns the death of singer-songwriter Dolly Parton, who died on August 25, 2026, at age 80, and honors her life and work. It recounts her rise from a large family in Sevier County, Tennessee, to one of the best-known figures in American music, and her founding of the Dollywood theme park. It highlights her charity work, including the Imagination Library, which mails free books to young children, millions of dollars in aid to families after the 2016 Sevier County wildfires, support for children's medical research, and bald eagle conservation. The Senate offers condolences to her family and encourages Americans to follow her example of kindness and service. It does not change any law or spending. As of September 17, 2026, the Senate had agreed to it.
for: Supporters say it is fitting for the Senate to honor someone whose music and generosity, especially her free-book program for young children, touched people across the country.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
